 16.Therefore to constitute an offense u/sec.420 IPC., there should not only be cheating, but as a consequence of such cheating, the accused should have dishonestly induced the person deceived to deliver any property to any person.

opennyai_summary.issue:
The points that arise for consideration are :
 1. Whether the prosecution has proved  beyond all reasonable doubt that  accused No.1 to 7 have committed the  offence U/s 420 r/w 34 of I.P.C. ?
 2. What order ?
 7.
The above points are answered as under :
 Point No.1: In the Negative.
15.Before discussing the facts and evidence of both parties, it is better to know the essential ingredients of Section - 420 of IPC :
 (i)Deception of a person either by making a  false or misleading representation or by  dishonest concealment or by any other act  or omission;
 (ii)Fraudulent or dishonest inducement of Veeranna vs Nirmalamma And Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129021907/
10  that person to either deliver any property or  14 C.C. No.15196/2012  to consent to the retention thereof by any  person or to intentional induce that person  so deceived to do or omit to do anything  which he would not do or omit if he were not  so deceived; and  (ii) Such act or omission causing or is  likely to cause damage or harm to that  person in body, mind, reputation or  property.
 16.Therefore to constitute an offense u/sec.420 IPC., there should not only be cheating, but as a consequence of such cheating, the accused should have dishonestly induced the person deceived to deliver any property to any person.
 17.In the light of above ingredients, let me discuss whether the prosecution is able to prove the ingredients of Sec.420 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
PW.1, who is a Sub-Registrar has no personal knowledge about the case as well as Ex.P1 to 3 and PW.2 and 3, who are the sons of CW.1/ Complainant though stated regarding the case of prosecution, their evidence clearly establishes schedule mentioned in the sale agreement and in the sale deed dated 25.09.1977 are altogether different and entire evidence placed by prosecution is only a hearsay evidence and during the course of evidence, witnesses have admitted that there is dispute regarding boundary and civil cases are pending in respect of said property.
When such being the case,
the question of attracting the provisions of Section - 420 IPC does not arise at all.
Accused have dealt with the property as their own property and by oversight the sale deed registration number was wrongly mentioned in the sale agreement, which was entered with the accused -7 and subsequently it was rectified by the accused .
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the main contention  15 C.C. No.15196/2012 of complainant that the accused -1 to 6 herein by referring his property bearing No.1760/1977-1978 dated 25.09.1977 have entered into an agreement of Veeranna vs Nirmalamma And Others on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129021907/
11 sale with the accused -7 in order to cheat him and they have executed the sale agreement though they have no right or title over the said property and as such they have committed the offenses u/sec.420 of IPC.
 18.On perusal of entire evidence on record, it shows that it is not the case of complainant that any of the accused tried to deceive him either by making a false or misleading representation or by any other action or omission, nor it is his case that they offered him any fraudulent or dishonest inducement to deliver any property or to consent to retention thereof by any person or they intentionally induce him to do or omit to do anything which he would not to do or omit if he were not so deceived.
Nor did the  16 C.C. No.15196/2012 complainant alleged that accused -1 to 6 pretended to be the complainant while executing the sale agreement.
Therefore it cannot be said that the accused -1 to 6 by the act of executing sale agreement in favour of accused -7 or accused -7 by reason of being the purchaser or the agreement holder with regard to the sale agreement deceived the complainant in any manner.
When a sale deed is executed conveying a property claiming ownership thereto, it may be possible for the purchaser under such sale deed, to allege that the  18 C.C. No.15196/2012 vendor has cheated him by making a false representation of ownership and fraudulently induced him to part with the sale consideration.
But in this case, the complaint is not a purchaser.
On the other hand, the purchaser is made a co-accused.
19. In the present case also, accused purchaser is not complainant.
On the other hand, he made as accused -7.
So, applying the above ratio as the purchaser is not the complainant, for cheating offence u/sec. 420 of IPC., cannot be attracted.
Therefore, in this view also the act done by accused persons by mistake is not an offense and it was done only by mistake and it comes under general exceptions of IPC under Chapter - IV.
 22 C.C. No.15196/2012
as discussed above, it is not the case where the complainant said to have been induced by the accused - 1 to 6 to enter into a transaction so as to deceive him with a view to cause unlawful loss to him and make unlawful gain for themselves.
On perusal of entire allegations in the complaint, there is no such ingredients for the offense punishable under section - 420 of IPC and complainant failed to show prima-facie materials regarding inducement and accused have made false representation and on the said false representation he acted with the property etc.,
As discussed above, any of the accused tried to deceive the complainant either by making a false or misleading representation or by any other action or omission nor it is his case that they offered him any fraudulent or dishonest inducement to deliver any property or to consent to retention thereof  25 C.C. No.15196/2012 by any person or they intentionally induce him to do or omit to do anything which he would not to do or omit if he were not so deceived.
So, in the absence of such materials the oral evidence and documentary evidence placed by prosecution is of no use.
Therefore, this court is of the opinion that prosecution not proved the ingredients of Section - 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
I have gone through the decisions relied by learned counsel for accused i.e., reported in 2007 AIR SCW 6332 Anil Ritolia Vs. State of Bihar and 2009 AIR SCW 307 V.Y. Jose Vs. State of Gujarat &
Ors; wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court while considering the ingredients of Section - 420 IPC has held that, for constituting an offense of cheating the complainant is required to show that the accused had fraudulent or dishonest intention at the time of making promise or representation.
